query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a surface coating of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy without any surface treatment.
generation.conditions: High-temperature conditions (above 1000°C) in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
generation.structural_mediator: Aluminum oxide layer acting as a protective barrier.
generation.mechanism: The aluminum oxide coating forms a stable, adherent layer that prevents oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy, thereby reducing oxidation rates.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated refractory high-entropy alloy will exhibit significantly lower weight gain due to oxidation compared to the untreated alloy after exposure to high-temperature oxygen conditions.
generation.baseline: Weight gain due to oxidation of untreated refractory high-entropy alloy at high temperatures.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys exposed to temperatures above 1000°C in an oxygen-rich environment.
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the aluminum oxide coating may vary depending on the specific composition of the high-entropy alloy and the coating application method.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a comparative study where one set of refractory high-entropy alloy samples is coated with aluminum oxide and another set remains untreated. Both sets will be exposed to an oxygen-rich atmosphere at 1100°C for 100 hours.
measurements: Weight gain due to oxidation measured before and after exposure
Microstructural analysis of the surface and subsurface layers
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the weight gain of the coated samples is not significantly lower than that of the untreated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
